task: T1: create specs/lib/assert.sh, the assertion vocabulary every gate in this repo will source. It is sourced, never executed, so it must not call `exit` at the top level and must not run anything on load. Define exactly two reporting functions: `ok` prints two spaces, `PASS`, two spaces and its argument to stdout; `no` prints two spaces, `FAIL`, two spaces and its argument to stderr and sets a variable `fail` to 1. Initialise `fail` to 0 at load. Define `gate_tmpdir`, which creates a temp directory into the variable `T`, writes a trivial executable script into it and runs it to prove the directory is not mounted noexec — if it cannot, print a single line naming the environment as the cause and exit 2, because a gate that cannot execute is neither a pass nor a fail and must not be reported as either. `gate_tmpdir` must also export `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` and point `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` inside `T`, so that running Python under a gate cannot leave a `__pycache__` in the tree the next scope check will measure. Define `gate_done`, which prints a `---` separator and then exits 0 printing `VERIFY: PASS` when `fail` is 0, or exits 1 printing `VERIFY: FAIL` otherwise. Do NOT define a `pend` function: a per-task gate asserts only its own task's criteria, so it has nothing to defer, and providing the verb is what invites the misfiled assertion this whole spec exists to remove. After this file is sourced, `pend` must not be callable. Do write a header comment naming the omission and its reason, so the absence reads as deliberate rather than forgotten — the ban is on defining the function, not on mentioning it in prose. Touch no other file; T2 owns the loop and T3 owns the self-test.
